./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:5886:712.21a If a melded permanent is put into its owner’s graveyard or library, that player may arrange the two cards in any order. If it’s put into its owner’s library, that player doesn’t reveal the order.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:5888:712.21b If a player exiles a melded permanent, that player determines the relative timestamp order of the two cards at that time. This is an exception to the procedure described in rule 613.7m.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:5897:Example: Leyline of the Void is an enchantment that reads, in part, “If a card would be put into an opponent’s graveyard from anywhere, exile it instead.” Wheel of Sun and Moon is an Aura with enchant player and the ability “If a card would be put into enchanted player’s graveyard from anywhere, instead that card is revealed and put on the bottom of its owner’s library.” If the controller of Chittering Host is affected by both cards’ effects, that player chooses one effect to apply to the event and Midnight Scavengers and Graf Rats are both moved to the appropriate zone.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:5941:714.3b As a player’s precombat main phase begins, that player puts a lore counter on each Saga they control with one or more chapter abilities. This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:5965:715.3d Instead of putting a spell that was cast as an Adventure into its owner’s graveyard as it resolves, its controller exiles it. For as long as that card remains exiled, that player may play it. It can’t be cast as an Adventure this way, although other effects that allow a player to cast it may allow a player to cast it as an Adventure.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:5997:717.2b In limited play, an Attraction deck must contain at least three Attraction cards from that player’s card pool, and may contain multiple Attractions cards with the same English name.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6007:717.6a Each card owned by the same player that has been put in the command zone this way is kept in a single face-up pile separate from any player’s Attraction deck. This pile is informally referred to as that player’s “junkyard.” The pile is not its own zone.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6089:722.1. Some cards allow a player to control another player during that player’s next turn. This effect applies to the next turn that the affected player actually takes. The affected player is controlled during the entire turn; the effect doesn’t end until the beginning of the next turn.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6099:722.4. If information about an object in the game would be visible to the player being controlled, it’s visible to both that player and the controller of the player. If information about cards outside the game would be visible to the player being controlled, it’s visible only to that player, not the controller of the player.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6100:Example: The controller of a player can see that player’s hand and the face of any face-down creatures they control.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6103:Example: The controller of another player decides which spells that player casts and what those spells target, and makes any required decisions when those spells resolve.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6104:Example: The controller of another player decides which of that player’s creatures attack, which player or planeswalker each one attacks, and how those attacking creatures assign their combat damage.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6106:722.5a The controller of another player can use only that player’s resources (cards, mana, and so on) to pay costs for that player.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6109:722.5b The controller of another player can’t make choices or decisions for that player that aren’t called for by the rules or by any objects. The controller also can’t make any choices or decisions for the player that would be called for by the tournament rules.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6112:722.6. The controller of another player can’t make that player concede. A player may concede the game at any time, even if they are controlled by another player. See rule 104.3a.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6156:724.2. There are two inherent triggered abilities associated with being the monarch. These triggered abilities have no source and are controlled by the player who was the monarch at the time the abilities triggered. This is an exception to rule 113.8. The full texts of these abilities are “At the beginning of the monarch’s end step, that player draws a card” and “Whenever a creature deals combat damage to the monarch, its controller becomes the monarch.”
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6160:724.4. If the monarch leaves the game, the active player becomes the monarch at the same time as that player leaves the game. If the active player is leaving the game or if there is no active player, the next player in turn order who can become the monarch becomes the monarch. If no player still in the game can become the monarch, the game continues with no monarch.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6168:725.2. There are three inherent triggered abilities associated with having the initiative. These triggered abilities have no source and are controlled by the player who had the initiative at the time the abilities triggered. This is an exception to rule 113.8. The full text of these abilities are “At the beginning of the upkeep of the player who has the initiative, that player ventures into Undercity,” “Whenever one or more creatures a player controls deal combat damage to the player who has the initiative, the controller of those creatures takes the initiative,” and “Whenever a player takes the initiative, that player ventures into Undercity.” See rule 701.49, “Venture into the Dungeon.”
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6172:725.4. If the player who has the initiative leaves the game, the active player takes the initiative at the same time that player leaves the game. If the active player is leaving the game or if there is no active player, the next player in turn order takes the initiative.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6183:Example: A player casts Living Wish, bringing a creature card into the game from outside the game. Then that game is restarted. The creature card will be part of that player’s library when the new game begins.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6185:726.3. Because each player draws seven cards when the new game begins, any player with fewer than seven cards in their library will lose the game when state-based actions are checked during the upkeep step of the first turn, regardless of any mulligans that player takes. (See rule 704, “State-Based Actions.”)
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6199:727.1. Rad counters are a kind of counter a player can have (see rule 122, “Counters”). There is an inherent triggered ability associated with rad counters. This ability has no source and is controlled by the active player. This is an exception to rule 113.8. The full text of this ability is “At the beginning of each player’s precombat main phase, if that player has one or more rad counters, that player mills a number of cards equal to the number of rad counters they have. For each nonland card milled this way, that player loses 1 life and removes one rad counter from themselves.”
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6213:728.2a As a subgame begins, if one or more supplementary decks of nontraditional cards are being used, each player moves each of their supplementary decks from the main-game command zone to the subgame command zone and shuffles it. (Face-up nontraditional cards remain in the main-game command zone.)
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6215:728.2b As a subgame of a Vanguard game starts, each player moves their vanguard card from the main-game command zone to the subgame command zone.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6217:728.2c As a subgame of a Commander game starts, each player moves their commander from the main-game command zone (if it’s there) to the subgame command zone.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6219:728.3. Because each player draws seven cards when a game begins, any player with fewer than seven cards in their deck will lose the subgame when state-based actions are checked during the upkeep step of the first turn, regardless of any mulligans that player takes. (See rule 704, “State-Based Actions.”)
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6227:728.5. At the end of a subgame, each player takes all traditional cards they own that are in the subgame other than those in the subgame command zone, puts them into their main-game library, then shuffles them. This includes cards in the subgame’s exile zone and cards that represent phased-out permanents as the subgame ends. Except as specified in rules 728.5a–c, all other objects in the subgame cease to exist, as do the zones created for the subgame. The main game continues from the point at which it was discontinued: First, the spell or ability that created the subgame finishes resolving, even if it was created by a spell card that’s no longer on the stack. Then, if any main-game abilities triggered while the subgame was in progress due to cards being removed from the main game, those abilities are put onto the stack.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6230:728.5a At the end of a subgame, each nontraditional card not in a supplementary deck that began the subgame in a supplementary deck is turned face down and put on the bottom of that deck. Then each player moves each of their supplementary decks from the subgame command zone to the main-game command zone and shuffles it.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6232:728.5b At the end of a subgame of a Vanguard game, each player moves their vanguard card from the subgame command zone to the main-game command zone. This is an exception to rule 313.2.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6234:728.5c At the end of a subgame of a Commander game, each player moves their commander from the subgame command zone (if it’s there) to the main-game command zone.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6266:729.3a If a merged permanent is put into its owner’s graveyard or library, that player may arrange the new objects in any order. If it’s put into its owner’s library, that player doesn’t reveal the order.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6268:729.3b If a player exiles a merged permanent, that player determines the relative timestamp order of the cards at that time. This is an exception to the procedure described in rule 613.7m.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6294:731.1a The rules for taking shortcuts are largely informal. As long as each player in the game understands the intent of each other player, any shortcut system they use is acceptable.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6306:Example: The active player draws a card during her draw step, then says, “Go.” The nonactive player is holding Into the Fray (an instant that says “Target creature attacks this turn if able”) and says, “I’d like to cast a spell during your beginning of combat step.” The current proposed shortcut is that all players pass priority at all opportunities during the turn until the nonactive player has priority during the beginning of combat step.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6308:731.2c Once the last player has either accepted or shortened the shortcut proposal, the shortcut is taken. The game advances to the last proposed ending point, with all game choices contained in the shortcut proposal having been taken. If the shortcut was shortened from the original proposal, the player who now has priority must make a different game choice than what was originally proposed for that player.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6310:731.3. Sometimes a loop can be fragmented, meaning that each player involved in the loop performs an independent action that results in the same game state being reached multiple times. If that happens, the active player (or, if the active player is not involved in the loop, the first player in turn order who is involved) must then make a different game choice so the loop does not continue.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6322:732.1. If a player takes an illegal action or starts to take an action but can’t legally complete it, the entire action is reversed and any payments already made are canceled. No abilities trigger and no effects apply as a result of an undone action. If the action was casting a spell, the spell returns to the zone it came from. Each player may also reverse any legal mana abilities that player activated while making the illegal play, unless mana from those abilities or from any triggered mana abilities they caused to trigger was spent on another mana ability that wasn’t reversed. Players may not reverse actions that moved cards to a library, moved cards from a library to any zone other than the stack, caused a library to be shuffled, or caused cards from a library to be revealed.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6338:800.4a When a player leaves the game, all objects (see rule 109) owned by that player leave the game and any effects which give that player control of any objects or players end. Then, if that player controlled any objects on the stack not represented by cards, those objects cease to exist. Then, if there are any objects still controlled by that player, those objects are exiled. This is not a state-based action. It happens as soon as the player leaves the game. If the player who left the game had priority at the time they left, priority passes to the next player in turn order who’s still in the game.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6341:Example: Alex casts Bribery, which reads, “Search target opponent’s library for a creature card and put that card onto the battlefield under your control. Then that player shuffles their library,” targeting Bianca. Alex puts Serra Angel onto the battlefield from Bianca’s library. If Bianca leaves the game, Serra Angel also leaves the game. If, instead, Alex leaves the game, Serra Angel is exiled.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6355:800.4g If an object requires a player who has left the game to make a choice other than whether to pay a cost, the controller of the object chooses another player to make that choice. If the original choice was to be made by an opponent of the controller of the object, that player chooses another opponent if possible.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6359:800.4i If an effect requires information about a specific player, the effect uses the current information about that player if they are still in the game; otherwise, the effect uses the last known information about that player before they left the game. If an effect requires information from the game about actions players have taken, the effect can find actions that were taken by a player who has left the game.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6365:800.4m When a player leaves the game, any continuous effects with durations that last until that player’s next turn or until a specific point in that turn will last until that turn would have begun. They neither expire immediately nor last indefinitely.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6367:800.4n When a player leaves the game, objects that player owns in the ante zone do not leave the game. This is an exception to rule 800.4a. See rule 407, “Ante.”
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6373:800.6. In a multiplayer game, the first mulligan a player takes doesn’t count toward the number of cards that player will put on the bottom of their library or the number of mulligans that player may take. Subsequent mulligans are counted toward these numbers as normal.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6381:801.2. A player’s range of influence is the maximum distance from that player, measured in player seats, that the player can affect. Players within that many seats of the player are within that player’s range of influence. Objects controlled by players within a player’s range of influence are also within that player’s range of influence. Range of influence covers spells, abilities, effects, damage dealing, attacking, making choices, and winning the game.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6389:801.2c The particular players within each player’s range of influence are determined as each turn begins.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6392:801.2d An object is within a player’s range of influence if it’s controlled by that player or by another player within that many seats of that player. In addition, a battle is within a player’s range of influence if it’s protected by that player or by another player within that many seats of that player.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6394:801.3. Creatures can attack only opponents within their controller’s range of influence, planeswalkers controlled by those opponents, and battles protected by those opponents. If no opponents are within a player’s range of influence, creatures that player controls can’t attack.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6396:801.4. Objects and players outside a player’s range of influence can’t be the targets of spells or abilities that player controls.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6404:Example: Alex, who has a range of influence of 2, is seated to the left of Rob, and Carissa, who has a range of influence of 1, is seated to the right of Rob. Alex casts a spell that reads, “An opponent chooses one — You draw two cards; or each creature you control gets +2/+2 until end of turn,” and chooses Carissa to make that choice. Carissa can choose the mode even though Alex is out of her range.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6422:Example: In a six-player game in which each player has range of influence 1, Alex casts Pyroclasm, which reads, “Pyroclasm deals 2 damage to each creature.” Pyroclasm deals 2 damage to each creature controlled by Alex, the player to Alex’s left, and the player to Alex’s right. No other creatures are dealt damage.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6425:Example: In a six-player game where each player has range of influence 1, Alex controls Coat of Arms, which reads, “Each creature gets +1/+1 for each other creature on the battlefield that shares at least one creature type with it.” Coat of Arms will boost Alex’s creatures based only on what creatures are controlled by Alex, the player to Alex’s left, and the player to Alex’s right. It won’t take other creatures into account.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6440:801.14. If an effect states that a player wins the game, all of that player’s opponents within that player’s range of influence lose the game instead.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6442:801.15. If the effect of a spell or ability states that the game is a draw, the game is a draw for that spell or ability’s controller and all players within that player’s range of influence. They leave the game. All remaining players continue to play the game.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6444:801.16. If the game somehow enters a “loop” of mandatory actions, repeating a sequence of events with no way to stop, the game is a draw for each player who controls an object that’s involved in that loop, as well as for each player within the range of influence of any of those players. They leave the game. All remaining players continue to play the game.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6456:802.2a Any rule, object, or effect that refers to a “defending player” refers to one specific defending player, not to all of the defending players. If an ability of an attacking creature refers to a defending player, or a spell or ability refers to both an attacking creature and a defending player, then unless otherwise specified, the defending player it’s referring to is the player that creature is attacking, the controller of the planeswalker that creature is attacking, or the protector of the battle that player is attacking. If that creature is no longer attacking, the defending player it’s referring to is the player that creature was attacking before it was removed from combat, the controller of the planeswalker that creature was attacking before it was removed from combat, or the protector of the battle that player was attacking before it was removed from combat. If a spell or ability could apply to multiple attacking creatures, the appropriate defending player is individually determined for each of those attacking creatures. If there are multiple defending players that could be chosen, the controller of the spell or ability chooses one.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6461:802.3a Restrictions and requirements that don’t apply to attacking a specific player are evaluated based on the entire group of attacking creatures. Restrictions and requirements that apply to attacking a specific player apply only to creatures attacking that player. The entire group of attacking creatures must still be legal. See rule 508.1.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6467:802.4a A defending player can block only with creatures they control. Those creatures can block only creatures attacking that player, a planeswalker that player controls, or a battle that player protects.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6477:803.1a If the attack left option is used, a player can attack only an opponent seated immediately to their left, a planeswalker that player controls, or a battle that player protects. If a player’s nearest opponent to the left is more than one seat away, the player can’t attack.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6479:803.1b If the attack right option is used, a player can attack only an opponent seated immediately to their right, a planeswalker that player controls, or a battle that player protects. If a player’s nearest opponent to the right is more than one seat away, the player can’t attack.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6495:805.3a The process for handling mulligans is altered accordingly. First, each player on the starting team, in whatever order that team likes, declares whether that player will take a mulligan. Then the players on each other team in turn order do the same. Teammates may consult while making their decisions. Then all mulligans are taken at the same time. Teammates may consult while choosing which cards, if any, to put on the bottom of their library. A player may take a mulligan even after a teammate has decided to keep their opening hand. See rule 103.5.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6497:805.3b The process for handling cards that allow a player to begin the game with them on the battlefield is altered accordingly. First, each player on the starting team, in whatever order that team likes, may put any or all such cards onto the battlefield from that player’s opening hand. Teammates may consult while making their decisions. Then each player on each other team in turn order does the same.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6499:805.4. Each team takes turns rather than each player.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6503:805.4b Each player on a team draws a card during that team’s draw step.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6507:805.4d An ability that triggers at the beginning of a step or phase may trigger multiple times if it triggers at the beginning of “each player’s” or “each opponent’s” step or phase. These abilities trigger once for each appropriate player if the ability’s trigger condition, effect, or intervening “if” clause refers to “that player,” “that opponent,” or similar.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6515:805.6. The Active Player, Nonactive Player order rule (see rule 101.4) is modified if the shared team turns option is used. If multiple teams would make choices and/or take actions at the same time, first the active team makes any choices required, then each nonactive team in turn order makes any choices required. If multiple players would make choices and/or take actions at the same time, first each player on the active team makes any choices required in whatever order they like, then the players on each nonactive team in turn order do the same. Once all choices have been made, the actions happen simultaneously.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6517:805.6a If more than one player is instructed to draw cards in a game that’s using the shared team turns option, first each player on the active team, in whatever order that team likes, performs that player’s draws, then each player on each nonactive team in turn order does the same.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6521:805.8. If an effect gives a player an extra turn or adds a phase or step to that player’s turn, that player’s team takes the extra turn, phase, or step. If an effect causes a player to skip a step, phase, or turn, that player’s team does so. If a single effect causes more than one player on the same team to add or skip the same step, phase, or turn, that team adds or skips only that step, phase, or turn. If an effect causes a player to control another player, the first player controls the affected player’s team.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6527:805.10a Each team’s creatures attack the other team as a group. During the combat phase, the active team is the attacking team and each player on the active team is an attacking player. Likewise, the nonactive team is the defending team and each player on the nonactive team is a defending player.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6545:806.2a The limited range of influence option usually isn’t used in Free-for-All games. If it is, each player has the same range of influence, which is determined before play begins. See rule 801, “Limited Range of Influence Option.”
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6572:807.4b The starting player in the game gets the first turn marker. The player four seats to that player’s left (the fifth player) takes the second turn marker, and so on until all the turn markers have been handed out. Each turn marker is assigned a number in this way. Then all players with turn markers start their turns at the same time.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6574:807.4c After a player ends their turn, that player passes the turn marker to the player on their left. If a player with a turn marker leaves the game during their turn, the player to their left takes the turn marker after that turn ends. If a player with a turn marker leaves the game before their turn begins, the player to their left takes the turn marker immediately.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6576:807.4d A player who receives a turn marker can’t begin their turn if any player in the three seats to their left has a turn marker. If this is the case, that player waits until the player four seats to their left takes the other turn marker.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6578:807.4e If a player leaves the game and that player leaving the game would reduce the number of turn markers in the game, the turn marker immediately to the departed player’s right is designated for removal. If more than one player leaves the game simultaneously, those players leaving the game would reduce the number of turn markers in the game, and there are multiple turn markers that could be removed, the marker with the lowest number is designated for removal. A turn marker may be designated for removal multiple times.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6586:807.4i If an effect causes a player with a turn marker to take an extra turn after the current one, that player keeps the turn marker and starts their next turn after the current turn ends, unless another turn marker is too close on either side at that time. If a turn marker is within three seats on the player’s left, the extra turn waits to begin until the player four seats to their left takes the other turn marker. If a turn marker is within three seats on the player’s right, the player passes the turn marker to their left when the turn ends rather than keeping it, and the player will take the extra turn immediately before their next turn.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6588:807.4j If an effect would cause a player to take an extra turn after the current turn, but that player wouldn’t have a turn marker at the start of that turn, that player will take the extra turn immediately before their next turn instead.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6638:809.6. The Emperor variant can also be played with any number of equally sized teams. If the teams have more than three players, the range of influence of each player should be adjusted.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6663:810.8a Players win and lose the game only as a team, not as individuals. If either player on a team loses the game, the team loses the game. If either player on a team wins the game, the entire team wins the game. If an effect says that a player can’t win the game, that player’s team can’t win the game. If an effect says that a player can’t lose the game, that player’s team can’t lose the game.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6664:Example: In a Two-Headed Giant game, a player controls Transcendence, which reads, in part, “You don’t lose the game for having 0 or less life.” If that player’s team’s life total is 0 or less, that team doesn’t lose the game.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6665:Example: In a Two-Headed Giant game, a player attempts to draw a card while there are no cards in that player’s library. That player loses the game, so that player’s entire team loses the game.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6666:Example: In a Two-Headed Giant game, a player controls Platinum Angel, which reads, “You can’t lose the game and your opponents can’t win the game.” Neither that player nor their teammate can lose the game while Platinum Angel is on the battlefield, and neither player on the opposing team can win the game.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6674:810.9. Damage, loss of life, and gaining life happen to each player individually. The result is applied to the team’s shared life total.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6675:Example: In a Two-Headed Giant game, a player casts Flame Rift, which reads, “Flame Rift deals 4 damage to each player.” Each team is dealt a total of 8 damage.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6679:Example: In a Two-Headed Giant game, a player controls Test of Endurance, an enchantment that reads, “At the beginning of your upkeep, if you have 50 or more life, you win the game.” At the beginning of that player’s upkeep, the player’s team wins the game if their team’s life total is 50 or more.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6680:Example: In a Two-Headed Giant game, a player on a team that has 11 life controls Lurking Evil, an enchantment that reads, “Pay half your life, rounded up: Lurking Evil becomes a 4/4 Horror creature with flying.” To activate the ability, that player must pay 6 life. The team winds up at 5 life.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6684:810.9c If an effect sets a single player’s life total to a specific number, the player gains or loses the necessary amount of life to end up with the new total. The team’s life total is adjusted by the amount of life that player gained or lost.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6685:Example: In a Two-Headed Giant game, a player on a team that has 25 life is targeted by an ability that reads, “Target player’s life total becomes 10.” That player’s life total is considered to be 25, so that player loses 15 life. The team winds up at 10 life.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6687:810.9d If an effect would set the life total of each player on a team to a number, that team chooses one of its members. On that team, only that player is affected.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6692:810.9f If an effect instructs a player to redistribute any number of players’ life totals, that player may not affect more than one member of each team this way.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6694:810.9g If an effect says that a player can’t gain life, no player on that player’s team can gain life.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6696:810.9h If an effect says that a player can’t lose life, no player on that player’s team can lose life or pay any amount of life other than 0.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6698:810.10. Effects that cause players to get poison counters happen to each player individually. The poison counters are shared by the team.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6700:810.10a If an effect needs to know how many poison counters an individual player has, that effect uses the number of poison counters that player’s team has. If an effect needs to know how many poison counters a player’s opponents have, that effect uses the number of poison counters opposing teams have.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6702:810.10b If an effect says that a player loses poison counters, that player’s team loses that many poison counters.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6704:810.10c If an effect says that a player can’t get poison counters, no player on that player’s team can get poison counters.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6706:810.10d If a rule or effect needs to know what kinds of counters an individual player has, that effect uses the kinds of counters that player has and the kinds of counters that player’s team has. A player is “poisoned” if that player’s team has one or more poison counters.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6708:810.11. The Two-Headed Giant variant can also be played with equally sized teams of more than two players. For each player a team has beyond the second, that team’s starting life total is increased by 15 and the number of poison counters required for the team to lose is increased by five. (These variants are called Three-Headed Giant, Four-Headed Giant, and so on.)
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6744:901.3. In addition to the normal game materials, each player needs a supplementary planar deck of at least ten plane and/or phenomenon cards and the game needs one planar die. No more than two cards in a planar deck can be phenomenon cards. Each card in a planar deck must have a different English name. (See rule 311, “Planes,” and rule 312, “Phenomena.”)
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6760:901.9. Any time the active player has priority and the stack is empty, but only during a main phase of their turn, that player may roll the planar die. Taking this action costs a player an amount of mana equal to the number of times they have previously taken this action on that turn. This is a special action and doesn’t use the stack. Note that this number won’t be equal to the number of times the player has rolled the planar die that turn if an effect has caused the player to roll the planar die that turn. (See rule 116.2i.)
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6770:901.10. When a player leaves the game, all objects owned by that player except abilities from phenomena leave the game. (See rule 800.4a.) If that includes a face-up plane card or phenomenon card, the planar controller turns the top card of their planar deck face up. This is not a state-based action. It happens as soon as the player leaves the game.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6776:901.11. After the game has started, if a player moves the top card of their planar deck off that planar deck and turns it face up, that player has “planeswalked.” Continuous effects with durations that last until a player planeswalks end. Abilities that trigger when a player planeswalks trigger. See rule 701.31.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6782:901.11c If a player planeswalks when there is more than one face-up plane card, that player planeswalks away from all such planes.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6798:901.14a Before the first turn of the game of the game, each player who will start the game with a turn marker sets a starting plane (see rule 901.5). Each of them is a planar controller.

./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6812:902.1. In the Vanguard variant, a vanguard card allows each player to play the role of a famous character. ./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6816:902.3. In addition to the normal game materials, each player needs a vanguard card. Each vanguard card is placed face up next to its owner’s library before the game begins. All vanguard cards remain in the command zone throughout the game.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6823:902.5a If a player takes a mulligan in a Vanguard game, just like in a normal game, that player shuffles their hand back into their library, then draws a new hand equal to their starting hand size. ./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6827:Example: The hand modifier of a player’s vanguard card is -1. That player’s maximum hand size is six. If that player has more than six cards in their hand as their cleanup step begins, they will discard all but six of them.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6844:903.3b If a player’s commander is a meld card and it’s melded with the other member of its meld pair, the resulting melded permanent is that player’s commander.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6846:903.3c If a player’s commander is a component of a merged permanent, the resulting merged permanent is that player’s commander.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6850:903.3e If an effect refers to a characteristic of “your commander,” it can find the appropriate player’s commander and see its current characteristics, as modified by continuous effects and other rules, in all zones, including that player’s library and hand.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6866:903.4f If an ability refers to the colors or number of colors in a commander’s color identity, that quality is undefined if that player doesn’t have a commander. That part of the ability won’t do anything. Costs that refer to that quality are unpayable.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6882:903.6. At the start of the game, each player puts their commander from their deck face up into the command zone. Then each player shuffles the remaining cards of their deck so that the cards are in a random order. Those cards become the player’s library.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6884:903.7. Once the starting player has been determined, each player sets their life total to 40 and draws a hand of seven cards.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6902:903.11a If a player is allowed to bring a card from outside the game into a Commander game, that player can’t bring a card into the game this way if it has the same name as a card that player had in their starting deck, if it has the same name as a card that the player owns in the current game, or if any color in its color identity isn’t in the color identity of the player’s commander.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6914:903.12e If a player’s commander has no colors in its color identity, that player’s deck may contain any number of basic lands of one basic land type of their choice. This is an exception to rule 903.5d.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6916:903.12f In a two-player Brawl game, each player’s starting life total is 25. In a multiplayer Brawl game, each player’s starting life total is 30.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6918:903.12g In any Brawl game, the first mulligan a player takes doesn’t count toward the number of cards that player will put on the bottom of their library or the number of mulligans that player may take. ./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6926:903.13b A draft typically consists of three draft rounds. In each draft round, each player opens a booster pack, drafts two cards by placing them in a face-down pile in front of them, then passes the remaining cards to the next player. Each player then drafts two cards from the booster pack passed to them and passes the remaining cards. This procedure continues until all cards in that draft round have been drafted.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6928:903.13c In the first and third draft rounds, booster packs are passed to each player’s left. In the second draft round, booster packs are passed to each player’s right.
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6932:903.13e After the draft is complete, the cards a player drafted become that player’s card pool. If the draft contained draft boosters from Commander Legends or Commander Masters, each player may add up to two cards named The Prismatic Piper to their card pool, but only if those cards are used as the player’s commander(s). If the draft contained draft boosters from Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur’s Gate®, each player may add up to two cards named Faceless One to their card pool, but only if those cards are used as the player’s commander(s).
./backend/rules/MagicCompRules.txt:6934:903.13f Commander Draft deck construction follows the same rules as Commander deck construction (see rule 903.5) with three exceptions: (1) A player’s deck must contain at least 60 cards. There is no maximum deck size. (2) A player’s deck may include any number of cards from that player’s card pool with the same name. (3) If the draft contained draft boosters from Commander Masters, any card which can be a player’s commander by itself and whose color identity includes one or fewer colors is considered to have the partner ability for the purposes of deckbuilding. (See rule 702.124, “Partner.”)

package cards

import (
	"testing"
)

// TestToilParse verifies the Toil half of Toil // Trouble (PIO):
// "Target player draws two cards and loses 2 life."
func TestToilParse(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	p := NewParser()

	oracleText := "Target player draws two cards and loses 2 life."

	result := p.Parse(oracleText, "Sorcery")

	if len(result.ParseErrors) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected parse errors: %v", result.ParseErrors)
	}

	var draw, loseLife *AbilityDSL
	for i := range result.Abilities {
		a := &result.Abilities[i]
		if a.Type != "spell" {
			continue
		}
		switch a.Effect {
		case "draw":
			draw = a
		case "player_loses_life":
			loseLife = a
		}
	}

	if draw == nil {
		t.Fatalf("missing draw spell effect; got %+v", result.Abilities)
	}
	if amt, _ := draw.Value["amount"].(int); amt != 2 {
		t.Errorf("draw: want amount 2, got %v", draw.Value["amount"])
	}
	if draw.Target == nil || draw.Target.Filter != "player" {
		t.Errorf("draw: want Target player, got %+v", draw.Target)
	}

	if loseLife == nil {
		t.Fatalf("missing player_loses_life spell effect; got %+v", result.Abilities)
	}
	if amt, _ := loseLife.Value["amount"].(int); amt != 2 {
		t.Errorf("player_loses_life: want amount 2, got %v", loseLife.Value["amount"])
	}
	if loseLife.Target == nil || loseLife.Target.Filter != "player" {
		t.Errorf("player_loses_life: want Target player, got %+v", loseLife.Target)
	}
}

// TestTroubleParse verifies the Trouble half of Toil // Trouble (PIO):
// "Trouble deals damage to target player equal to the number of cards in that player's hand."
func TestTroubleParse(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	p := NewParser()

	oracleText := "Trouble deals damage to target player equal to the number of cards in that player's hand."

	result := p.Parse(oracleText, "Sorcery")

	if len(result.ParseErrors) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected parse errors: %v", result.ParseErrors)
	}

	var damage *AbilityDSL
	for i := range result.Abilities {
		a := &result.Abilities[i]
		if a.Type == "spell" && a.Effect == "damage" {
			damage = a
		}
	}

	if damage == nil {
		t.Fatalf("missing damage spell effect; got %+v", result.Abilities)
	}
	if src, _ := damage.Value["amount_source"].(string); src != "target_hand_size" {
		t.Errorf("damage: want amount_source target_hand_size, got %v", damage.Value["amount_source"])
	}
	if damage.Target == nil || damage.Target.Filter != "player" {
		t.Errorf("damage: want Target player, got %+v", damage.Target)
	}
}

// Metamorphic Blast (OTJ), Instant, {U}:
//
//	"Spree (Choose one or more additional costs.)
//	 + {1} — Until end of turn, target creature becomes a white Rabbit with base power and toughness 0/1.
//	 + {3} — Target player draws two cards."
//
// Regression for task-5758: Spree header and + {cost} — mode lines produced parse_errors.
func TestParser_MetamorphicBlast_Spree(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	p := NewParser()
	def := &CardDefinition{
		Name: "Metamorphic Blast",
		Type: "Instant",
		Text: "Spree (Choose one or more additional costs.)\n+ {1} — Until end of turn, target creature becomes a white Rabbit with base power and toughness 0/1.\n+ {3} — Target player draws two cards.",
	}
	p.ParseCard(def)

	if len(def.ParseErrors) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("expected no parse errors, got %v", def.ParseErrors)
	}

	var spreeAb *AbilityDSL
	for i := range def.Abilities {
		if def.Abilities[i].Type == "keyword_cost" && def.Abilities[i].Effect == "spree" {
			spreeAb = &def.Abilities[i]
			break
		}
	}
	if spreeAb == nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected keyword_cost/spree ability, got abilities: %+v", def.Abilities)
	}
}

// patternTargetPlayerDrawsCards matches the simple "Target player draws N cards." form.
// Example: Can't Quite Recall (MB2)
func patternTargetPlayerDrawsCards() *Pattern {
	return &Pattern{
		ID:          "target_player_draws_cards",
		Name:        "Target Player Draws Cards",
		Description: "Target player draws N cards",
		Examples:    []string{"Can't Quite Recall"},
		Regex:       regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^Target player draws (\w+|\d+) cards?\.?$`),
		CardTypes:   []string{"Instant", "Sorcery"},
		Priority:    50,
		Template: func(matches []string, cardType string) []AbilityDSL {
			amount := parseWordNumber(matches[1])
			return []AbilityDSL{
				{
					Type:   "spell",
					Effect: "draw",
					Value:  map[string]interface{}{"amount": amount},
					Target: &TargetFilter{Filter: "player"},
				},
			}
		},
	}
}

// patternTargetPlayerDrawsCardsAndLosesLife matches "Target player draws N cards and loses N life."

func patternTargetPlayerDrawsCardsAndLosesLife() *Pattern {
	return &Pattern{
		ID:          "target_player_draws_cards_and_loses_life",
		Name:        "Target Player Draws Cards and Loses Life",
		Description: "Target player draws N cards and loses N life",
		Examples:    []string{"Toil"},
		Regex:       regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^Target player draws (\w+|\d+) cards? and loses (\d+|\w+) life\.?$`),
		CardTypes:   []string{"Instant", "Sorcery"},
		Priority:    44,
		Template: func(matches []string, cardType string) []AbilityDSL {
			drawAmount := parseWordNumber(matches[1])

			return []AbilityDSL{
				{
					Type:   "spell",
					Effect: "draw",

					Target: &TargetFilter{Filter: "player"},
				},
				{
					Type:   "spell",
					Effect: "player_loses_life",
					Value:  map[string]interface{}{"amount": lifeAmount},
					Target: &TargetFilter{Filter: "player"},
				},
			}
		},
	}
}

// mapTriggerToEventType maps DSL trigger strings to EventType
func mapTriggerToEventType(trigger string) game.EventType {
	switch trigger {
	case "enters_battlefield", "etb":
		return game.EventEntersBattlefield
	case "dies":
		return game.EventDies
	case "exiled":
		return game.EventExiled
	case "attacks":
		return game.EventAttacks
	case "blocks":
		return game.EventDeclareBlocker
	case "deals_combat_damage":
		return game.EventDealsCombatDamage
	case "deals_damage_to_player":
		return game.EventDealsPlayerDamage
	case "untap_step":
		return game.EventUntapStep
	case "upkeep", "upkeep_start":
		return game.EventUpkeepStart
	case "main_phase", "main_phase_start":
		return game.EventMainPhase
	case "end_step":
		return game.EventEndStep
	case "draw":
		return game.EventDrawCard
	case "spell_cast":
		return game.EventSpellCast
	case "when_cast":
		return game.EventSpellCast
	case "when_cast_from_exile":
		return game.EventSpellCastFromExile
	case "spell_cast_from_graveyard":
		return game.EventSpellCastFromGraveyard
	case "targeted", "becomes_target":
		// EventTargeted is declared but NEVER published; the live event is
		// EventBecomesTarget (becomes_target.go, wired in dispatch round 2).
		return game.EventBecomesTarget
	case "life_gain":
		return game.EventLifeGain
	case "tapped", "becomes_tapped":
		return game.EventTapped
	case "untapped", "becomes_untapped":
		return game.EventUntapped // publish sites wired in dispatch round 2
	case "beginning_of_combat":
		return game.EventCombatStart // engine string is combat_start; old name was inert (57 v1 records)
	case "monstrous", "becomes_monstrous":
		return game.EventBecomesMonstrous
	case "exploited", "exploit":
		return game.EventExploit
	case "leaves_battlefield", "ltb":
		return game.EventLeavesBattlefield
	case "transforms_into", "transforms":
		return game.EventTransform
	// task-2453 (event_unsupported:gy_enter_anywhere): "gy_enter_anywhere"
	// (Bloodchief Ascension/Sefris of the Hidden Ways class, "a card is put
	// into [your/an opponent's] graveyard from anywhere") was in
	// V2TriggerEvents but never wired to a live engine event — the default
	// pass-through converted it to EventType("gy_enter_anywhere"), which
	// nothing published (inert). The engine now publishes EventEntersGraveyard
	// ("enters_graveyard") from the AddCard-side zone-agnostic chokepoint
	// (zone.go publishGraveyardEnter) — same fix shape as plays_land above.
	case "gy_enter_anywhere":
		return game.EventEntersGraveyard
	default:
		// Pass dynamic event type strings through directly (e.g. "becomes_level_2"
		// fired by Class enchantment level-up in class.go).
		return game.EventType(trigger)
	}
// Package cards - DSL Type Definitions
// Defines all types used for card ability representation
package cards

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"magic-backend/game"
	"time"
)

// ============================================================================
// CARD STATUS
// ============================================================================

// CardStatus represents the review status of a card definition
type CardStatus string

const (
	StatusAutoParsed  CardStatus = "auto"        // Parser erfolgreich
	StatusNeedsReview CardStatus = "review"      // Parser unsicher, braucht Review
	StatusManual      CardStatus = "manual"      // Manuell korrigiert
	StatusVerified    CardStatus = "verified"    // Geprüft & freigegeben
	StatusUnsupported CardStatus = "unsupported" // Nicht unterstützt (zu komplex)
)

// ============================================================================
// ABILITY DSL
// ============================================================================

// AbilityDSL represents a parsed ability in DSL format
type AbilityDSL struct {
	Type    string                 `json:"type"`              // static, triggered, activated, spell
	Effect  string                 `json:"effect"`            // pump, grant, damage, draw, destroy, etc.
	Value   map[string]interface{} `json:"value,omitempty"`   // {power: 1, toughness: 1}
	Keyword string                 `json:"keyword,omitempty"` // for grant effects
	Trigger string                 `json:"trigger,omitempty"` // etb, dies, attacks, upkeep
	Cost    *AbilityCost           `json:"cost,omitempty"`    // for activated abilities
	Affects *TargetFilter          `json:"affects,omitempty"` // who is affected
	Target  *TargetFilter          `json:"target,omitempty"`  // targeting requirements

	// ---- Paragraph Schema v2 (docs/paragraph-schema-v2.md, adapter step 3a) ----
	// All optional; absent on every v1 record. Use DerivedTrigger()/
	// DerivedEffects() to read the v2 view regardless of record generation.
	TriggerV2 *TriggerSpec `json:"trigger_v2,omitempty"` // factored trigger object (Change 1)
	Effects   []EffectAtom `json:"effects,omitempty"`    // ordered effect sequence (Change 3)
	Condition *Condition   `json:"condition,omitempty"`  // "as long as ..." for statics (Change 2)
}

// AbilityCost represents the cost of an activated ability
type AbilityCost struct {
	Tap            bool          `json:"tap,omitempty"`
	Untap          bool          `json:"untap,omitempty"` // {Q} — untap this permanent as cost
	Mana           game.ManaCost `json:"mana,omitempty"`
	Sacrifice      string        `json:"sacrifice,omitempty"`       // "creature", "permanent", "self", etc.
	SacrificeCount int           `json:"sacrifice_count,omitempty"` // number to sacrifice (default 1, e.g. "Sacrifice two Blood tokens")
	Life           int           `json:"life,omitempty"`
	Energy         int           `json:"energy,omitempty"`       // Pay N {E} (Rule 106.11)
	DiscardSelf    bool          `json:"discard_self,omitempty"` // Discard this card (Channel etc.)
	DiscardN       int           `json:"discard_n,omitempty"`    // Discard N cards as cost
	DiscardHand    bool          `json:"discard_hand,omitempty"` // Discard your hand as cost (e.g. Lion's Eye Diamond)
	MillN          int           `json:"mill_n,omitempty"`       // Mill N cards from your own library as cost (e.g. "Mill a card:", "Mill two cards:")
	Additional     string        `json:"additional,omitempty"`   // "tap_another_creature", "discard", etc.
	Restriction    string        `json:"restriction,omitempty"`  // "metalcraft", "threshold:3:artifact", etc.

	// TapOther: "Tap another/an untapped X you control" — a SINGLE permanent,
	// chosen by the activating player (a real choice — see
	// game.ActivationCost.TapOther), as opposed to TapOthers below which
	// taps a fixed COUNT where which ones is not a meaningful choice.
	// Closed-vocabulary string, "_"-joined (matchSimpleTapType): base type
	// (creature/artifact/land/enchantment/planeswalker/permanent),
	// "legendary" qualifier, a color name, or a subtype — e.g.
	// "legendary_creature", "blue_creature", "wizard".
	TapOther string `json:"tap_other,omitempty"`

	// ReturnOther: "Return a/an/another X you control to its owner's hand"
	// as an activation cost — the SINGLE-permanent, player-chosen sibling
	// of ReturnToHand below (which carries a TargetFilter+Count but is not
	// wired to game.ActivationCost at all — no declarative pathway exists
	// for a non-self return-to-hand cost). Same closed vocabulary as
	// TapOther (game.ActivationCost.ReturnOther / matchesReturnOtherType,
	// which reuses matchSimpleTapType), just without the untapped
	// requirement — e.g. "artifact", "land", "legendary_creature".
	ReturnOther string `json:"return_other,omitempty"`

	// ---- Paragraph Schema v2 cost extensions (Change 6, adapter step 3a) ----
	RemoveCounters *CounterCost   `json:"remove_counters,omitempty"` // Remove N TYPE counters from X
	TapOthers      *TapOthersCost `json:"tap_others,omitempty"`      // Tap N untapped X you control
	ExileCost      *ExileCost     `json:"exile,omitempty"`           // Exile self/N cards from zone
	ReturnToHand   *ReturnCost    `json:"return_to_hand,omitempty"`  // Return X to owner's hand
	Tag            string         `json:"tag,omitempty"`             // exhaust|boast|forecast|... (closed)
	RestrictionV2  string         `json:"restriction_v2,omitempty"`  // V2CostRestrictions enum
	Condition      *Condition     `json:"cost_condition,omitempty"`  // "Activate only if ..."

	// CostReductionSpec — "This ability costs {N} less to activate for each
	// X" (task-1980 static_cost_mod). Same closed dynamic count-spec shape
	// as an effect atom's value.amount_count (game/dynamic_amount.go
	// EvalDynamicAmount); passed through verbatim onto
	// game.ActivationCost.CostReductionSpec, which resolves it fresh at
	// both canPayAbilityCost and payAbilityCost time.
	CostReductionSpec map[string]interface{} `json:"cost_reduction_spec,omitempty"`
}

// TargetFilter defines what a spell/ability affects or targets
type TargetFilter struct {
	Filter     string `json:"filter,omitempty"`     // creature, permanent, player, spell
	Subtype    string `json:"subtype,omitempty"`    // Vampire, Zombie, etc.
	Color      string `json:"color,omitempty"`      // W, U, B, R, G
	Controller string `json:"controller,omitempty"` // you, opponent, any
	// Owner is the OWNERSHIP counterpart of Controller ("Commander
	// creatures you OWN" — grant_nested_triggered round, task-2373): "you"
	// = owned by the ability's controller. Distinct from Controller when a
	// permanent is stolen. Only read by the grant_nested_triggered
	// converter branch so far.
	Owner string `json:"owner,omitempty"`
	// Attached scopes a nested-ability grant to the single permanent the
	// granting card is attached to ("Enchanted creature has ..." /
	// "Equipped creature has ..." — static_grant_quoted attachment family,
	// task-2421). Only the grant_nested_triggered/grant_nested_activated
	// converter branches read it (onto GrantRecipientFilter.Attached);

./scripts/skills/primitive-catalog.md:298:- `DiscardEachPlayer(gs *game.GameState, n int)` (cardfns/lib_discard_each_player.go) — every player in `gs.Players` discards n cards, auto-selecting the first n cards in each player's hand order (no interactive chooser exists, matching `Discard`'s behavior). Loops `gs.Discard(i, ...)` per player, mirroring `MillEachPlayer`'s per-player loop over `gs.Mill`; still routes through `GameState.Discard` so `game.EventDiscard` fires per discarded card (reachable via `OnDiscard`/`OnYouDiscard` above). Discarding more than a player's hand size discards as many as possible without error (Rule 701.8a). **[dur: one-shot — discards once at call time, no lingering effect]**
./scripts/skills/primitive-catalog.md:975:- `ChoosePlayerOption(gs *game.GameState, playerIdx int, options []string, sourceName string, resolve func(gs *game.GameState, chosen string))` (cardfns/lib_choose_option.go) — opens the choice (sets `gs.PendingOptionChoice`); `resolve` fires once playerIdx answers, with the engine having no notion of what a chosen option "does" — apply the card-specific effect (e.g. `SkipNextDraw`/`SkipNextCombat`, see `skip_combat_phase`/`skip_draw_step`) yourself inside `resolve`.
./scripts/skills/primitive-catalog.md:1133:- `OnEachPlayerUpkeep(gs *game.GameState, self *game.Card, action func(gs *game.GameState, self *game.Card, playerIdx int) )` (cardfns/lib_each_player_upkeep_trigger.go) — "at the beginning of each player's upkeep" (not just yours). Subscribes to `game.EventUpkeepStart` WITHOUT the `e.Player == self.Controller` filter that `OnUpkeep` applies; `playerIdx` is the player whose upkeep it is, so a handler can target "that player's" permanents. Requires `self` still be on the battlefield. For "at the beginning of **your** upkeep," use the companion `OnUpkeep` below instead. **[dur: n/a — fires once per qualifying upkeep, no lingering effect]**

    m = re.match(rf'^up to ({NUM}) (?:other|another) target (.+)$', l)

// Converts CardDefinitions to game.Card instances
package cards

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"magic-backend/game"
)

// ToGameCard converts a CardDefinition to a game.Card
func (def *CardDefinition) ToGameCard(owner int) (*game.Card, error) {
	var cardType game.CardType
	switch def.Type {
	case "Land":
		cardType = game.TypeLand
	case "Creature":
		cardType = game.TypeCreature
	case "Instant":
		cardType = game.TypeInstant
	case "Sorcery":
		cardType = game.TypeSorcery
	case "Artifact":
		cardType = game.TypeArtifact
	case "Enchantment":
		cardType = game.TypeEnchantment
	case "Planeswalker":
		cardType = game.TypePlaneswalker
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown card type: %s", def.Type)
	}

	// Create the card based on type
	var card *game.Card
	if def.Type == "Land" {
		card = game.NewLand(def.Name, def.LandType, owner)
	} else if def.Type == "Creature" {
		power := 0
		toughness := 0
		if def.Power != nil {
			power = *def.Power
		}
		if def.Toughness != nil {
			toughness = *def.Toughness
		}
		card = game.NewCreature(def.Name, def.ManaCost, power, toughness, owner)
	} else if def.Type == "Instant" {
		// Check for spell effect in abilities
		spellEffect := def.GetSpellEffect()
		def.liftSecondaryTokenEffect(spellEffect)
		def.liftSecondaryLifeGainEffect(spellEffect)
		def.liftSecondaryEndTurnEffect(spellEffect)
		if spellEffect != nil {
			card = game.NewInstant(def.Name, def.ManaCost, spellEffect, owner)
		} else {
			card = game.NewCard(def.Name, cardType, def.ManaCost, owner)
		}
	} else if def.Type == "Sorcery" {
		// Check for spell effect in abilities
		spellEffect := def.GetSpellEffect()
		def.liftSecondaryTokenEffect(spellEffect)
		def.liftSecondaryLifeGainEffect(spellEffect)
		def.liftSecondaryEndTurnEffect(spellEffect)
		if spellEffect != nil {
			card = game.NewSorcery(def.Name, def.ManaCost, spellEffect, owner)
		} else {
			card = game.NewCard(def.Name, cardType, def.ManaCost, owner)
		}
	} else {
		card = game.NewCard(def.Name, cardType, def.ManaCost, owner)
	}

	// Set additional properties
	card.SubTypes = def.SubTypes
	card.Types = append([]string(nil), def.Types...)
	card.Colors = def.Colors
	card.ColorIdentity = def.ColorIdentityOf()
	card.IsBasic = def.IsBasic
	card.Keywords = def.Keywords
	// Rebound (Rule 702.87a/87b, [VOCAB] keyword_args import-gate): the
	// printed keyword must set Card.ReboundData itself — gamestate.go's
	// post-resolution routing only exiles-then-recasts via
	// card.ReboundData.HasRebound, which previously only came from a
	// one-shot grant (cardfns.GrantReboundToCastSpell), never from this
	// bare keyword. Without this, a card whose ONLY rebound source is the
	// printed keyword would parse but silently go to the graveyard like any
	// other spell.
	if card.HasKeyword(game.Rebound) {
		card.ReboundData = &game.ReboundData{HasRebound: true}
	}
	card.Protection = append([]game.ProtectionQuality(nil), def.Protection...)
	card.HexproofFrom = append([]game.HexproofColorQuality(nil), def.HexproofFrom...)
	card.Text = def.Text
	card.Legendary = def.Legendary

	// Initialise loyalty counters for planeswalkers (Rule 306.5b).
	if def.Type == "Planeswalker" && def.StartingLoyalty > 0 {
		card.Counters.Loyalty = def.StartingLoyalty
	}

	// Convert and attach abilities from DSL
	def.attachAbilities(card)

	// cant_be_blocked_by_relative_power_self primitive (ticket #3452,
	// REPARSE-MAP static_unmapped / "Creatures with power less than ~'s
	// power can't block it" family, e.g. Aura Gnarlid, Battering Wurm):
	// cardfns/DenProtector.go proves this restriction already works end to
	// end through cardfns.RestrictBlockersTo, but only as a bespoke
	// per-card CardHandler keyed by exact card name — precisely because no
	// registered primitive expressed the clause. This bridges the SAME
	// mechanism onto the DSL: a static ability atom naming this effect
	// registers an equivalent closure into game.CardHandlers for THIS
	// card's own name, so any carddb entry can carry the clause without a
	// hand-written CardHandler of its own.
	for _, ab := range def.Abilities {
		if ab.Type != "static" {
			continue
		}
		for _, atom := range ab.Effects {
			if CanonicalEffect(atom.Effect) != "cant_be_blocked_by_relative_power_self" {
				continue
			}
			cardName := def.Name
			game.CardHandlers[cardName] = func(gs *game.GameState, self *game.Card) {
				if RestrictBlockersToFn == nil {
					return
				}
				RestrictBlockersToFn(gs, func(attacker *game.Card) bool {
					return attacker.ID == self.ID
				}, func(attacker, blocker *game.Card) bool {
					return blocker.GetPower() >= attacker.GetPower()
				})
			}
		}
	}

	// v2 multi-atom spells (re-parse R1r7): a spell-type ability with an
	// Effects sequence resolves through the R0c walker instead of the
	// single-SpellEffect path.
	if def.Type == "Instant" || def.Type == "Sorcery" {
		for i, ab := range def.Abilities {
			if ab.Type != "spell" || len(ab.Effects) == 0 {
				continue
			}
			for ai, atom := range ab.Effects {
				// "Exile ~." as one step of a v2 sequence (task-1922, e.g.
				// "Discard your hand, then draw eight cards. ~ deals 8
				// damage to each opponent. Exile ~." — Blood for the Blood
				// God!): the resolving spell isn't a battlefield permanent,
				// so the ordinary "exile" executor (executeExileEffect,
				// battlefield RemoveCard) would silently find nothing and
				// no-op. Bridge onto the same SelfExile field the v1
				// single-effect path (buildMainSpellEffect's "exile" case,
				// above) and Eldritch Evolution/Time Stop already use —
				// gamestate.go's resolution-time exileOnResolve check reads
				// it regardless of which path built card.SpellEffect, and
				// the SpellEffectSequence branch runs in preference to the
				// SpellEffect branch (gamestate.go's else-if chain), so
				// setting both fields here doesn't cause a double-dispatch.
				// Not appended as a sequence atom — there's nothing for the
				// walker to execute.
				if self, ok := atom.Value["self"].(bool); ok && self && CanonicalEffect(atom.Effect) == "exile" {
					if card.SpellEffect == nil {
						card.SpellEffect = &game.SpellEffect{}
					}

// primary effect is something else (Ultima: destroy all artifacts and
// creatures, then end the turn; Day's Undoing: shuffle+draw, then
// conditionally end the turn). A standalone "End the turn." (Time Stop) is
// already handled directly by buildMainSpellEffect's "end_turn" case, so
// this only fires when the primary effect matched an EARLIER ability.
func (def *CardDefinition) liftSecondaryEndTurnEffect(eff *game.SpellEffect) {
	if eff == nil {
		return
	}
	spellCount := 0
	for _, ab := range def.Abilities {
		if ab.Type != "spell" || ab.Effect == "surveil" {
			continue
		}
		spellCount++
		if spellCount > 1 && ab.Effect == "end_turn" {
			eff.EndsTurn = true
			if cond, ok := ab.Value["condition"].(string); ok {
				eff.EndsTurnCondition = cond
			}
			return
		}
	}
}

// liftSecondaryTokenEffect scans def.Abilities for a second spell ability of
// type "create_token" and, if found, copies its value map into
// eff.CreateTokenEffect. Called after GetSpellEffect to pick up trailing
// token-creation effects (e.g. Malevolent Rumble's Eldrazi Spawn).
func (def *CardDefinition) liftSecondaryTokenEffect(eff *game.SpellEffect) {
	if eff == nil {
		return
	}
	spellCount := 0
	for _, ab := range def.Abilities {
		if ab.Type != "spell" || ab.Effect == "surveil" {
			continue
		}
		spellCount++
		if spellCount > 1 && (ab.Effect == "create_token" || ab.Effect == "token") {
			eff.CreateTokenEffect = copyValueMap(ab.Value)
			return
		}
	}
}

// GetSpellEffect extracts the spell effect from abilities (for instants/sorceries).
// Surveil and gain_energy abilities are skipped in the main loop — surveil is
// lifted onto card.SurveilN in attachAbilities, and gain_energy is collected
// as a pre-effect and stored in SpellEffect.GainEnergyAmount.
func (def *CardDefinition) GetSpellEffect() *game.SpellEffect {
	// Collect any spell-type gain_energy pre-effect (e.g. Galvanic Discharge).
	gainEnergyAmount := 0
	for _, a := range def.Abilities {
		if a.Type == "spell" && a.Effect == "gain_energy" {
			if n := numToInt(a.Value["amount"]); n > 0 {
				gainEnergyAmount = n
			}
		}
	}

	eff := def.buildMainSpellEffect()
	if eff != nil && gainEnergyAmount > 0 {
		eff.GainEnergyAmount = gainEnergyAmount
	}
	return eff
}

// Shape behavioral tests (docs/review.md follow-up: "one test per SHAPE,
// not per record card"). Each trigger x effect combination the record tier
// uses is proven here ONCE, end-to-end through the real pipeline:
// AbilityDSL record -> ToGameCard -> RegisterCardAbilities -> event ->
// stack -> resolution -> observable game-state change. Individual record
// cards then need no behavioral test of their own — the record linter
// (carddb_lint_test.go) guarantees they only use shapes proven here.
//
// When a worker's SHAPE_DEMAND gets built, the builder adds the new
// shape's test to this file — that is part of what "building a shape"
// means (mirroring how a VOCAB primitive ships with its lib_*_test.go).

// shapeCard builds a minimal creature CardDefinition carrying the given
// abilities, converts it, puts it onto the battlefield, and returns the
// game plus the card. No carddb dependency — shapes are tested from
// records constructed inline.
func shapeCard(t *testing.T, abilities []AbilityDSL) (*game.GameState, *game.Card) {
	t.Helper()
	p, tough := 2, 2
	def := &CardDefinition{
		Name:      "Shape Test Subject",
		Type:      "Creature",
		Types:     []string{"Creature"},
		Power:     &p,
		Toughness: &tough,
		Abilities: abilities,
		Status:    StatusManual,
	}
	card, err := def.ToGameCard(0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ToGameCard: %v", err)
	}
	gs := game.NewGame("P0", "P1", false)
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		gs.Players[0].Library.AddCard(game.NewCard(fmt.Sprintf("Plains %d", i), game.TypeLand, game.ManaCost{}, 0))
	}
	gs.Battlefield.AddCard(card)
	gs.RegisterCardAbilities(card)
	return gs, card
}

// fire publishes an event, then resolves everything it put on the stack.
func fire(t *testing.T, gs *game.GameState, ev *game.Event) {
	t.Helper()
	gs.ProcessTriggeredAbilities(ev)
	for !gs.Stack.IsEmpty() {
		if err := gs.ResolveTopOfStack(); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("resolving trigger: %v", err)
		}
	}
}

func TestShape_ETB_Draw(t *testing.T) {
	gs, card := shapeCard(t, []AbilityDSL{
		{Type: "triggered", Trigger: "etb", Effect: "draw", Value: map[string]interface{}{"amount": 2}},
	})
	before := gs.Players[0].Hand.Count()
	fire(t, gs, game.CreateETBEvent(card, 0))
	if got := gs.Players[0].Hand.Count() - before; got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("etb->draw(2): expected 2 cards drawn, got %d", got)
	}
}

func TestShape_ETB_LifeGain(t *testing.T) {
	gs, card := shapeCard(t, []AbilityDSL{
		{Type: "triggered", Trigger: "etb", Effect: "life_gain", Value: map[string]interface{}{"amount": 3}},
	})
	before := gs.Players[0].Life
	fire(t, gs, game.CreateETBEvent(card, 0))
	if got := gs.Players[0].Life - before; got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("etb->life_gain(3): expected +3 life, got %+d", got)
	}
}

}

func TestShape_ETB_BecomeMonarch(t *testing.T) {
	gs, card := shapeCard(t, []AbilityDSL{
		{Type: "triggered", Trigger: "etb", Effect: "become_monarch"},
	})
	if game.IsMonarch(gs, 0) {
		t.Fatalf("expected player 0 not to be monarch before the trigger fires")
	}
	fire(t, gs, game.CreateETBEvent(card, 0))
	if !game.IsMonarch(gs, 0) {
		t.Fatalf("etb->become_monarch: expected controller to be the monarch")
	}
}

func TestShape_ETB_WinGame(t *testing.T) {
	gs, card := shapeCard(t, []AbilityDSL{
		{Type: "triggered", Trigger: "etb", Effect: "win_game"},
	})
	fire(t, gs, game.CreateETBEvent(card, 0))
	if !gs.GameOver || gs.Winner != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("etb->win_game: expected controller to win, GameOver=%v Winner=%d", gs.GameOver, gs.Winner)
	}
}

// put_counters, each-shape: "put a +1/+1 counter on each Elf you control".
// Was parser-emitted but executor-less (inert) before 3c round 1.
func TestShape_ETB_PutCountersEach(t *testing.T) {
	gs, card := shapeCard(t, []AbilityDSL{
		{Type: "triggered", Trigger: "etb", Effect: "put_counters", Value: map[string]interface{}{
			"counter_type": "+1/+1", "target": "each", "filter": "Elf", "controller": "you"}},
	})
	elf := game.NewCreature("Shape Elf", game.ManaCost{}, 1, 1, 0)
	elf.SubTypes = []string{"Elf"}
	gs.Battlefield.AddCard(elf)
	nonElf := game.NewCreature("Shape Bear", game.ManaCost{}, 2, 2, 0)
	gs.Battlefield.AddCard(nonElf)
	theirs := game.NewCreature("Their Elf", game.ManaCost{}, 1, 1, 1)
	theirs.SubTypes = []string{"Elf"}
	theirs.Controller = 1
	gs.Battlefield.AddCard(theirs)

	fire(t, gs, game.CreateETBEvent(card, 0))

	if elf.Counters.PlusOnePlusOne != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("your Elf: expected 1 +1/+1 counter, got %d", elf.Counters.PlusOnePlusOne)
	}
	if nonElf.Counters.PlusOnePlusOne != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("non-Elf must not get a counter, got %d", nonElf.Counters.PlusOnePlusOne)
	}
	if theirs.Counters.PlusOnePlusOne != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("opponent's Elf must not get a counter, got %d", theirs.Counters.PlusOnePlusOne)
	}
}

// TestThoughtKnotSeer_FullOracleText verifies that both the ETB exile and LTB
// draw triggers are parsed from the real Scryfall oracle text for Thought-Knot
// Seer. This guards against a regression where the LTB trigger was silently
// dropped because the cached card definition predated patternLTBOpponentDraw.
func TestThoughtKnotSeer_FullOracleText(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	p := NewParser()
	def := &CardDefinition{
		Name:      "Thought-Knot Seer",
		Type:      "Creature",
		Power:     intPtr(4),
		Toughness: intPtr(4),
		Text:      "When Thought-Knot Seer enters, target opponent reveals their hand. You choose a nonland card from it and exile that card.\nWhen Thought-Knot Seer leaves the battlefield, target opponent draws a card.",
	}
	p.ParseCard(def)

	hasETB, hasLTB := false, false
	for _, ab := range def.Abilities {
		if ab.Trigger == "etb" && ab.Effect == "exile_nonland_from_opponent_hand" {
			hasETB = true
		}
		if ab.Trigger == "ltb" && ab.Effect == "draw" {
			hasLTB = true
		}
	}
	if !hasETB {
		t.Errorf("missing ETB exile_nonland_from_opponent_hand; abilities: %+v", def.Abilities)
	}
	if !hasLTB {
		t.Errorf("missing LTB draw trigger; abilities: %+v", def.Abilities)

// TestLTBOpponentDrawTriggerFires verifies that Thought-Knot Seer's LTB trigger
// fires when the card leaves the battlefield and makes the opponent draw a card.
func TestLTBOpponentDrawTriggerFires(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	gs := game.NewGame("Player1", "Player2", true)
	p := NewParser()

	def := &CardDefinition{
		Name:      "Thought-Knot Seer",
		Type:      "Creature",
		Power:     intPtr(4),
		Toughness: intPtr(4),
		Text:      "When Thought-Knot Seer leaves the battlefield, target opponent draws a card.",
	}
	p.ParseCard(def)

	tks, err := def.ToGameCard(0) // controlled by player 0
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ToGameCard: %v", err)
	}

	// Give the opponent a card in their library so the draw effect can fire
	libCard := game.NewCreature("Dummy", game.ManaCost{}, 1, 1, 1)
	gs.Players[1].Library.AddCard(libCard)

	gs.Battlefield.AddCard(tks)
	gs.RegisterCardAbilities(tks)

	// Confirm the LTB trigger is registered
	if len(gs.EventBus.GetAbilitiesForCard(tks.ID)) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("expected at least 1 ability registered for TKS")
	}

	oppHandBefore := len(gs.Players[1].Hand.Cards)

	// Simulate TKS leaving the battlefield via an LTB event
	event := game.CreateLTBEvent(tks, tks.Controller)
	triggered := gs.EventBus.Publish(event)
	gs.EventBus.UnregisterAbilitiesFromCard(tks.ID)

	if len(triggered) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("expected LTB trigger to fire; got 0 triggered abilities")
	}

	// Put the triggered ability on the stack and resolve it
	for _, ab := range triggered {
		gs.PutTriggeredAbilityOnStack(ab)
	}
	if err := gs.ResolveTopOfStack(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ResolveTopOfStack: %v", err)
	}

	// Opponent (player 1) should have drawn 1 card
	oppHandAfter := len(gs.Players[1].Hand.Cards)
	if oppHandAfter != oppHandBefore+1 {
		t.Errorf("expected opponent hand size %d, got %d", oppHandBefore+1, oppHandAfter)
	}
}

import pathlib
import sys
import unittest


sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).parent))
import reparse  # noqa: E402


class DamageRecipientCountTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def map_damage(self, text):
        verb, args = reparse.O.parse_atom(text)
        self.assertEqual(verb, "damage")
        return reparse.map_atom(verb, args, kind="triggered")

    def test_each_player_uses_recipient_land_count(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            self.map_damage(
                "~ deals damage to each player equal to the number of lands they control."
            ),
            (
                "damage",
                {
                    "target": "each_player",
                    "each_player_amount_count": {
                        "count": "battlefield",
                        "filter": "land",
                        "controller": "you",
                    },
                },
                None,
            ),
        )

    def test_each_opponent_uses_recipient_land_count(self):
        effect, value, target = self.map_damage(
            "~ deals damage to each opponent equal to the number of lands they control."
        )
        self.assertEqual(effect, "damage")
        self.assertEqual(value["target"], "each_opponent")
        self.assertEqual(value["each_player_amount_count"]["controller"], "you")
        self.assertIsNone(target)

    def test_target_player_uses_targets_nonbasic_lands(self):
        effect, value, target = self.map_damage(
            "~ deals damage to target player equal to the number of nonbasic lands they control."
        )
        self.assertEqual(effect, "damage")
        self.assertTrue(value["each_player_amount_count"]["nonbasic"])
        self.assertEqual(target, {"filter": "player"})

    def test_upkeep_that_player_binds_event_player(self):
        result = reparse.reparse_card(reparse.load_card("Primal Order"))
        self.assertTrue(result["eligible"])
        effect = result["abilities"][0]["effects"][0]
        self.assertEqual(effect["effect"], "damage")
        self.assertEqual(effect["value"]["target_ref"], "event_player")
        self.assertTrue(
            effect["value"]["each_player_amount_count"]["nonbasic"]
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
